vignette: A 58-year-old man with atrial fibrillation has a stroke and afterward cannot repeat sentences, although he speaks fluently and understands everything; his speech contains sound substitutions that he corrects. MRI shows a small infarct in the left supramarginal white matter.
explanation: Conduction aphasia (fluent, comprehending, unable to repeat, self-corrected phonemic errors) is a disconnection of the posterior temporal from the frontal language cortex through the arcuate fasciculus, which runs beneath the supramarginal gyrus.
